class.name: SpringCast
class.brief_description: Simulates a spring physically connected to a main body, using a sphere shape cast.
class.description: [SpringCast] is intended to simulate things like legs, which will push off generally any surface and includes friction forces, for a single main body. [b]Note:[/b] SpringCast only collides with [PhysicsBody3D] objects, it will ignore [Area3D].

method.name: add_constraint
method.description: Adds the constraint to the physics simulation. The spring must also be [member enabled] to actually do anything.

method.name: add_exception
method.description: Add a collision exception with the given body.

method.name: add_exception_rid
method.description: Add a collision exception with the given RID.

method.name: clear_exceptions
method.description: Clear all collision exceptions. Note that SpringCast always ignores the main body no matter what.

method.name: get_angular_lambda
method.description: Get the total angular impulse force (N m s) applied as rotational friction. This only applies to body collisions that have multiple contact points.

method.name: get_collision_mask_value
method.description: Get the value of a specific collision mask layer.

method.name: get_contact_average_point
method.description: Get the average contact point of a body. There must be collisions to call this method.

method.name: get_contact_body
method.description: Get a contact body. There must be collisions to call this method.

method.name: get_contact_body_count
method.description: Get the number of contact bodies.

method.name: get_contact_body_rid
method.description: Get a contact body RID. There must be collisions to call this method.

method.name: get_contact_normal
method.description: Get the contact normal of a body. There must be collisions to call this method.

method.name: get_contact_point
method.description: Get a contact point by index. When providing only the point index, it indexes all contact points. When also providing a body index, it indexes contact points only on that body. When also providing a shape index, it indexes contact points only on that body's shape. There must be collisions to call this method.

method.name: get_contact_point_count
method.description: Get the total number of contact points. When providing a body index, it counts contact points only on that body. When also providing a shape index, it counts contact points only on that body's shape. There must be collisions to call this method.

method.name: get_contact_shape
method.description: Get the contact shape of a specific body. There must be collisions to call this method.

method.name: get_contact_shape_count
method.description: Get the number of contact shapes for a specific body. There must be collisions to call this method.

method.name: get_friction_lambda
method.description: Get the total impulse force (N s) applied as planar friction.

method.name: get_spring_lambda
method.description: Get the total impulse force (N s) applied by the spring.

method.name: get_spring_length
method.description: Get the current length of the spring. This will always be between 0.0 and the max length specified in settings.

method.name: has_hit_hard_point
method.description: Returns true if the spring has been compressed to its minimum length and applied rigid collision forces.

method.name: is_colliding
method.description: Returns true if the spring is touching another body.

method.name: is_constraint_added
method.description: Returns true if the spring is currently in the physics simulation. Also check [method is_enabled] to test if the spring is actually able to apply forces.

method.name: remove_constraint
method.description: Remove the constraint from the physics simulation. This can be slower than setting [member enabled] to [code]false[/code] for short durations. If the spring will be disabled for a while, this can improve performance over just setting [member enabled] to [code]false[/code].

method.name: remove_exception
method.description: Remove a collision exception with the given body.

method.name: remove_exception_rid
method.description: Remove a collision exception with the given RID.

method.name: set_collision_mask_value
method.description: Set the value of a specific collision mask layer.

method.name: set_enabled
method.description: Set the spring's active status. Active spring casts will collide and apply forces to bodies while they are in the physics simulation (see [method is_constraint_added]).

members.member: Whether the spring cast should automatically add itself to the physics simulation (see [method add_constraint]) when entering the scene tree, and automatically remove itself when exiting the scene tree. If this is [code]false[/code] before it enters the scene tree, then it will not be added to the physics simulation, and you must eventually call [method add_constraint] for it to do anything.
The collision mask of this spring cast, will only collide with bodies on these layers.

Color of the debug shape in game, used when the spring is not colliding with anything. The default color, transparent black [code]Color(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)[/code], causes the debug shape to be rendered using the color from [member ProjectSettings.debug/shapes/collision/shape_color].
The active status of the spring. When enabled and added to the physics simulation (see [method is_constraint_added]), it will collide and apply forces.

Path to the main body, this is the body that the spring is physically attached to and will receive impulse and friction forces from bodies that the spring collides with. [b]Note:[/b] The main body is ALWAYS ignored for collision shape cast. If for some reason you need it to intersect a part of the main body, you must break it into two parts and use joints to connect them.

A [Callable] that can be used to restrict which collisions are possible during spring cast collision testing. The spring first collides with all possible bodies within its range, selecting the nearest set of collision points for each body. The results are then passed to this user function to limit which bodies are kept during finalization. From that set, the collisions are pruned to only include collisions near the closest spring fraction. This means some bodies you return may not collide if their collisions are not within some distance of the closest spring fraction. [b]Note:[/b] Earlier RIDs in the returned list are not guaranteed to be kept over later RIDs according to the [SpringCastSettings.max_bodies] limit. You should therefore limit the size of the returned RIDs to that limit if you must ensure all bodies are collision candidates. This method is only provided to drop specific bodies before a finalization phase which selects the nearest set of collisions across all bodies. As an example, it can be used to ignore collisions that have extreme angles, potentially on closer bodies, in favor of collisions that have better angles, potentially on further bodies: [codeblocks] [gdscript] @export var max_preferred_slope: float = deg_to_rad(45.0)
func pick_collisions( rid_list: Array[RID], spring_fraction_list: PackedFloat32Array, average_contact_point_list: PackedVector3Array, average_normal_list: PackedVector3Array ) -> Array[RID]: # As a simple case, drop RIDs that exceed a preferred slope angle if any normal is within that angle # NOTE: you may set a higher maximum angle on the spring settings and use a lower angle here
var cos_preferred: float = cos(max_preferred_slope) var global_up: Vector3 = global_basis.y
var preferred: Array[RID] = Array() for i in range(average_normal_list.size()): var normal: Vector3 = average_normal_list[i] if normal.dot(global_up) >= cos_preferred: preferred.append(rid_list[i])
if preferred.size() > 0: return preferred
return rid_list [/gdscript] [/codeblocks]
The spring settings for this spring cast.
